title: Plans and counts
prompt: What does this program print? `orders` is the 12-row orders table from the lesson, with four paid orders.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

paid = orders.filter(F.col("status") == "paid")
two = paid.limit(2)
print(type(two).__name__)
print(two.count(), paid.count(), orders.count())
hints: `filter` and `limit` are transformations. What kind of object does a transformation give back?
A transformation makes a new DataFrame. It never changes the one it started from.
`count()` is an action: it runs each plan and counts its rows.
